_comment: Source families: what each table lets you see. A family is covered as soon as one of its members is fed; members of a family are equivalents (or complementary points of view). A member is a whole table (`tables`, or { table }) or part of a table: a channel (`security`: Security log, `sysmon`: Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon, `system`: Service Control Manager) and a list of EventIDs, or a free `where` filter. A logged table (SecurityEvent, WindowsEvent, Event) covers a family only if its events are actually collected: the coverage rule checks it member by member. Every table read by a rule must belong to a family (checked at build). An "optional" family enriches results (roles) without being an event source.

members.label: file access (SACL)
members.hint: Audit "File System" (Object Access) and audit SACLs on the folders to watch (shares, sensitive data, profiles); without a SACL no 4663 is produced. Matching advanced audit policy on the machines (and domain controllers), and collection of these IDs by the agent's data collection rule ("All" level or an XPath query).
